delta_from_v1_0: A deeper Lima museum sweep recovered a publicly catalogued Egyptian bronze-and-wood dagger attributed to Pharaoh Thutmose III in the Museo Oro del Peru y Armas del Mundo. This upgrades Lima from a purely diplomatic/museum-cooperation control to a city with at least one claimed original ancient-Egyptian object candidate. It does NOT connect Lima to Mendes 1902, CG 53469 / JE 35425, the stamped-gold djed, or a literal Osiris relic.

new_lima_antiquity_node.institution: Museo Oro del Peru y Armas del Mundo / Fundacion Miguel Mujica Gallo
new_lima_antiquity_node.object_public_label: Daga egipcia de bronce del faraon Tutmosis III
new_lima_antiquity_node.reported_marking: personal emblem of Pharaoh Thutmose III

source_1.finding: The official tourism inventory describes an Egyptian bronze-and-wood dagger bearing the personal emblem of Thutmose III and states that the museum holds registered original movable cultural-property pieces. The page does not expose an object-level accession number or acquisition provenance for the dagger.

source_2.authority: Museo Oro del Peru y Armas del Mundo official website
source_2.finding: The museum itself lists 'Daga egipcia de bronce del faraon Tutmosis III 1200 AC' in its Arms of the World display.

catalogue_inconsistency.issue: The official museum page labels the object as Thutmose III yet dates it to 1200 BC, centuries after Thutmose III's reign. MINCETUR gives Thutmose III's reign as 1479-1425 BC but does not provide the dagger's object date. This may be a simple label/date error, but until resolved it prevents high-confidence historical attribution.

osiris_relevance.reason: The object is currently an Egypt-in-Lima provenance/control witness only. No Mendes, Djedet, Osiris, djed, Nesbanebdjedet, Quibell, JE, CG, or 1902 connection is reported.

lima_egyptian_antiquity_inventory_proven.objective: Determine what genuine or claimed ancient-Egyptian objects are actually held in Lima collections, starting with the Thutmose III dagger, and reconstruct their acquisition/registration/documentation chains before testing any relationship to CROFT.
required_inputs: Museum inventory/accession number for the Thutmose III dagger
Exact object label and complete catalogue record
Peruvian Ministry of Culture registration identifier and registration date if applicable to this object
Dimensions, weight, bronze-alloy description and wood identification if available
Any Egyptological authentication or published specialist attribution
Any Egyptian export, loan, restitution or ownership documentation
Complete list of other Egyptian-labelled objects in Armas del Mundo or associated storage
lima_egyptian_antiquity_inventory_proven.pass_condition: Recover an object-level passport sufficient to distinguish authenticated antiquity, historically documented antiquarian acquisition, modern replica/reproduction, composite/restored object, or unresolved attribution.
lima_egyptian_antiquity_inventory_proven.strong_pass_condition: Recover both object-level provenance and independent Egyptological/material verification.
lima_egyptian_antiquity_inventory_proven.osiris_promotion_condition: Only cross into the Osiris/Mendes branch if an object-level source explicitly introduces Mendes/Djedet/Tell el-Ruba, Osiris, djed, Banebdjedet/Nesbanebdjedet, Quibell 1902, JE/CG/TR identifiers, or a custody chain intersecting known Mendes dispersal nodes.

institutional_corridor_evidence.note: Signed 2005-05-17; in force 2006-03-18. Provides a bilateral cultural-property protection/restitution framework.
Article 23 promotes museum contacts, conservation/research information exchange, specialist exchange, and exhibitions of representative archaeological pieces subject to museum collection rules.

osiris_mainline_firewall.main_target: Mendes 1902 / CG 53469 / JE 35425 + unresolved stamped-gold djed passport/body-coordinate problem
active_primary_tests: CG 53469 basal topology/seams and conservation history/current mass
Grouped-lot passport recovery if djed was never individualized

next_actions: Recover the Thutmose III dagger's object-level catalogue/passport and acquisition history.
Inventory all other Egyptian-labelled objects in the Museo Oro del Peru y Armas del Mundo collection before selecting any one as relevant.
Search for Osiris/djed/Mendes identifiers only after the Lima Egyptian-object inventory is source-bound.
Do not interrupt the Mendes CG53469/JdE/Engelbach mainline while the Lima provenance gate is unresolved.
Preserve the 1200 BC vs Thutmose III chronology discrepancy as an explicit authentication warning, not as evidence of fraud or modernity.
canonical_formula: LIMA_HAS_PUBLICLY_CATALOGUED_EGYPTIAN_ANTIQUITY_CANDIDATE AND PROVENANCE_AUTHENTICITY_OPEN AND NO_MENDES_OSIRIS_BINDING => OPEN_LIMA_OBJECT_PASSPORT_GATE; KEEP_MENDES_AS_MAINLINE
canonical_seal: LIMA JUST BECAME MORE INTERESTING: NOT BECAUSE OSIRIS WAS FOUND THERE, BUT BECAUSE A REAL OBJECT-LEVEL EGYPTIAN ANTIQUITY CLAIM EXISTS AND CAN NOW BE TESTED.
